strand: Time and Place: How did Canada become a country?
text: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: To gain territories, resources, and prestige (expansionism), European countries sent explorers overseas, for example: Jacques Cartier; Giovanni Caboto; Pierre Du Gua de Monts; Samuel de Champlain
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: First Nations and Europeans made treaties with each other, such as the Two Row Wampum (Gaswéñdah), to start a relationship of living side by side.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Colonies were transferred from France to Britain as a result of conflicts and treaties.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Britain gained control of Acadia (Treaty of Utrecht, 1713) and New France (Treaty of Paris, 1763) as the result of treaties signed between Britain and France.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: French colonists remained on the lands known as Acadia and New France after Britain gained control of the territories.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Acts were passed by the British to rule and organize colonies in North America.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: The Royal Proclamation (1763) has ongoing significance for First Nations today, including: recognition of First Nations as the original inhabitants of North America; recognition of First Nations right to self-government; establishment of nation-to-nation treaty making process; establishment of First Nations relations to the Crown
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: The Royal Proclamation and the Quebec Act impacted ways of living for: First Nations; French colonists; British colonists
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: The Royal Proclamation and the Quebec Act impacted ways of living, including: size and location of territories; religious and language rights; governance structure; land sale and use
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: The Quebec Act (1774) recognized French language and religious rights in the province of Quebec and provided a foundation for bilingualism in Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Wars, rivalries, and treaties in Europe disrupted life in the colonies.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: New acts and legislation set foundations for Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Compare reasons for exploration and establishing colonies around the world.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Discuss ways relationships were built between First Nations and Europeans.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Investigate the travels of an explorer to the land now known as Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Describe the shift in control of colonies in the land now known as Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Discuss the significance of the Royal Proclamation for First Nations.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Relate the Quebec Act to Francophone rights in Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: The Thirteen Colonies gained independence from Britain (American Revolution) and established the United States of America (1776).
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: After the United States of America became independent, a border with British North America was established (Treaty of Paris, 1783).
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Loyalists from the Thirteen Colonies (United Empire Loyalists) migrated to colonies in the land now known as Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: In response to the increase of Loyalists, the Crown divided the province of Quebec into Upper Canada and Lower Canada ( Constitution Act , 1791, Canada Act ).
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: British colonists, French colonists, First Nations, and Métis shared a common purpose of resisting American expansion in a series of battles over territory and trade in North America, known as the War of 1812.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: After the War of 1812, Britain encouraged people from England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland to migrate to the land now known as Canada during what is called the Great Migration (1815–50).
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: After Britain abolished slavery (1833), enslaved Black people from the United States of America migrated to the land now known as Canada with the support of the Underground Railroad.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Dissatisfaction over the balance of power between Anglophones and Francophones led to rebellions in Upper and Lower Canada (1837–38) and the creation of the Province of Canada ( Act of Union ), including: unification of Upper and Lower Canada to create one province of Canada; policies to assimilate Francophones; establishment of one responsible government with equal representation for Canada East and Canada West (Durham Report); designation of English as the official language of government
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Immigrants contributed to the foundation of Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Governments can make changes in response to the actions of the population.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Compare changes in political boundaries using maps of pre-Confederation Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Infer how migration influenced the balance of power in the land now known as Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Describe the role of the War of 1812 in building relationships between groups in the land now known as Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate changes in Canada’s political boundaries.
text: Investigate stories about the Underground Railroad.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Time and Place: How did colonies influence the formation of Canada?
text: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: France established permanent settlements on the land now known as Canada, including: Port-Royal (1605); Quebec City (1608); Trois-Rivières (1634); Montreal (1642)
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: Samuel de Champlain, who established Quebec City, became the governor of New France and made alliances with the First Nations of the area.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: France founded the colonies of Acadia, New France, and Louisiana, and Britain founded the Thirteen Colonies.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: Colonization involved European monarchs expanding empires by claiming land and establishing colonies on land already occupied by Indigenous peoples around the world, including in North America (imperialism).
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: Colonists came to the colonies for a variety of opportunities, for example: access to farmland; business; religious freedom; quality of life; adventure
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: Colonists brought belief systems and ways of organizing society to the colonies, including: religions; leadership; education; health care
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: France and Britain imported natural resources from the colonies in North America, for example: furs; lumber; agricultural products; minerals
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: The establishment of New France began European colonization of Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: Research French settlements in the land that is now known as the province of Quebec and explore the challenges in establishing settlements.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: Examine the challenges and contributions of immigrants before Confederation.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine significant historical events that contributed to the formation of the country of Canada.
text: Assess the relationship between home countries and colonies.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Systems: How is the government of Canada organized?
text: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: The structure of government in Canada evolved over time, was shaped by historical events and acts, and reflects British governance.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: Negotiations between the British colonies and the British government about a possible union of the colonies took place over several years (Charlottetown Conference, Quebec Conference, London Conference).
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: Negotiations involved debates about issues such as American expansionism and the construction of a railroad system.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: The Fathers of Confederation, including Anglophone and Francophone politicians, contributed to the negotiation of the British North America Act (1867), which is also known as the BNA Act or the Constitution Act of 1867 .
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: The BNA Act united the Province of Canada, which was renamed Ontario and Quebec, with New Brunswick and Nova Scotia to form the Dominion of Canada at Confederation in 1867.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: The BNA Act established the parliamentary system with Members of Parliament (MPs) as representatives, the prime minister as the leader, and a Governor General to represent the Crown (the sovereign).
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: Modern government reflects historical influences.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: Discuss reasons for negotiations that led to Confederation.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: Examine perspectives of Francophones and Anglophones on Confederation.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate historical influences on the federal government in Canada.
text: Describe the historical and modern significance of the British North America Act .
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Systems: How did economic opportunities influence the establishment of Canada?
text: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Through the fur trade, furs were shipped from North America to Europe, where supply was low, and manufactured goods were shipped from Europe to North America, where demand was high.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Competition for control of the fur trade motivated Europeans to: establish the Hudson's Bay Company and the North West Company; expand farther north and west by building more trading posts and forts
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Trading posts and forts were: centres for interactions such as meeting and bartering; warehouses for goods, supplies, and medicines; lodgings
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Roles of First Nations, Métis, and Europeans that contributed to the fur trade included: hunters and trappers; interpreters and guides; clerks; coureurs des bois and voyageurs
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Social and economic success of the fur trade relied on First Nations and Métis women, who were intermediaries between European traders and First Nations and Métis communities.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Trade can contribute to social and economic change.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Model the fur trade’s system of exchange.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Discuss interactions between First Nations, Métis, and Europeans that occurred as part of the fur trade.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students examine the role of the fur trade in the development of Canada.
text: Identify the contributions made by a woman, or a group of women, to the fur trade.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

text: Students investigate rights and responsibilities in Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate rights and responsibilities in Canada.
text: Citizenship in Canada carries responsibilities, such as contributing to the community, respecting the rights of others, and voting.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students investigate rights and responsibilities in Canada.
text: Citizens in Canada have rights, freedoms, and responsibilities.

strand: Students investigate rights and responsibilities in Canada.

sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Time and Place: How can history provide insight into modern democracies?
text: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Democracy originated in ancient Athens in response to authoritarian rule.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Democracies have fundamental principles, including: equality under law; justice; freedom; representation
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Direct democracy, where all male citizens were required to participate in government, originated in ancient Athens in response to authoritarian rule.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The structure of government may be influenced by geographical features, for example, geographical size or type of terrain.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Athens had three social classes with different rights and responsibilities: citizens; metics; slaves
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Citizens and non-citizens in ancient Athens and the Roman Republic were defined by social class.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Features of direct democracy from ancient Athens included: a lottery; the Draconian constitution; majority rule through voting; debate of proposed laws; secret ballots; separate government bodies ( Boule , Ecclesia , and Dikasteria ); equal political rights for male citizens, such as freedom of speech and political participation
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Representative democracy, in which elected citizens make decisions for society, was used in the provincia of the Roman Republic.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Male patricians and plebians could vote for a representative (magistrate) to the senate and assemblies.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The Roman Republic was composed of three branches of government based on the Constitution: executive: two consuls; legislative: senate and assemblies ( comitia centuriata , comitia tributa , comitia curiata , concilium plebis ); judicial: judges
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Athenian direct democracy and Roman representative democracy were limited by lack of efficiency and representation.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The Magna Carta (1215) limited absolute authority of the monarchy in medieval England (absolute monarchism).
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The Magna Carta provided a foundation for legal protection and individual rights, and the Habeas Corpus Act (1679) established individual legal rights.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The Magna Carta provided a foundation for accountability by requiring the monarch to consult with a council to make decisions, and the Bill of Rights (1689) granted parliament with authority to make decisions.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The Bill of Rights (1689) formalized civil and parliamentary rights such as free elections, meetings of parliament, and free speech in parliament.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The legacy of the Bill of Rights includes formalized legal rights and free debate in parliament.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: First Nations of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy use a government system in which multiple Nations continue to come together to make decisions through consensus.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The Grand Council is the meeting of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy where Chiefs represent the voices of each Nation in decision making.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Clan Mothers influence decision making through their role in the Haudenosaunee Confederacy.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The Great Law of Peace is a binding agreement that guides the Haudenosaunee Confederacy in establishing roles, decision-making procedures, and collective rights.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Democracy and democratic principles were significantly shaped by events in England.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Athenian democracy provided a foundation for citizenship and participation in contemporary society.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Democracy in the Roman Republic provided a foundation for representation in contemporary society.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: The Haudenosaunee Confederacy decision-making structure includes democratic principles.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Investigate the origin of democracy in ancient Athens.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Identify the similarities and differences between Athenian democracy and the Roman Republic.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Compare direct and representative democracy.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Discuss ways legislation and agreements have advanced principles of democracy.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students relate the foundational principles of democracy to government systems throughout time and place.
text: Explain roles of Chiefs and Clan Mothers in decision making in the Haudenosaunee Confederacy.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Systems: How are the principles of democracy part of governments in Canada?
text: Students analyze democracy in Canada.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students analyze democracy in Canada.
text: Government systems provide structure for societies through leadership, decision-making processes, and application of laws.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students analyze democracy in Canada.
text: Democracy is a government system in which citizens have a voice in decision making.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)

strand: Students analyze democracy in Canada.
text: Democracy in Canada is based on the structure of the British parliamentary system and reflects principles of democracy evident in earlier systems of government.
sourceTitle: Alberta Social Studies Kindergarten to Grade 6 (Alberta Education, 2024)
